text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Abdul Salam al-Majali meets deputies; says received a semi-official invitation to visit Damascus and expects elections to take place on time.
- A royal decree is passed which boosts allowances and benefits to the members of the state judiciary.
- Jordan participates in the Malta EU-Mediterranean conference; Jordanian envoy says Arab states will insist on incorporating a condemnation of Israel in the conference's proceedings.

- Five million dinars ($7 million) of losses incurred by Jordan Valley farmers in damage to their crops from the latest freezing weather; proposals to exempt them from loan interest and reschedule debts to ease their plight.
- Majali meets Canadian peace coordinator; says resolving the Palestinian refugee problem means attaining their national rights and setting up an independant Palestinian state.

- Majali tells deputies the government does not plan to dissolve parliament or hold an extraordinary session; says elections under the existing 1993 law is not ruled out. The opposition criticise the premier's meeting with the deputies and claim government's policies are not clear.
- Jordan River Bridge closed to passenger traffic on Thursday to mark the Moslem Eid al-Adha feast.

- First shipment of 52,000 tonnes of French wheat under the U.N.'s "oil-for-food" deal to be shipped to Iraq via the Red Sea port of Aqaba is expected to start offloading by Friday, port officials say.
- Crown Prince calls for a national strategy to develop Jordan.
- Government considers setting up a body to retrain public sector employees as part of administrative reforms to rehabilitate the bloated civil service.
- Majali meets 60 lower house deputies and promises close contact while a new election law is formulated.
- Crown prince says educational programmes should have a national identity.
